title: Durable agent-execution substrate hardens into a standard primitive by H1 2027
body: Two June launches landed within a day of each other and split the autonomous-coding-agent field along a single axis - not model quality, but where the long-running agent physically executes. On June 11 OpenAI acquired Ona, the rebranded Gitpod, and folded it into the Codex group precisely to run agents inside persistent cloud sandboxes that keep multi-day coding tasks alive after the developer's workstation powers off, with European trade coverage framing the durable, restart-surviving execution layer as the workflow Anthropic already dominates in the enterprise and the thing OpenAI is buying infrastructure and talent to contest. On June 12 Moonshot shipped Kimi Work, a downloadable desktop agent that takes the opposite bet: an always-on local Agent Swarm of roughly 300 sub-agents on the open-weight Kimi K2.6, driving the user's logged-in browser through a WebBridge extension and firing overnight jobs through a built-in cron engine with a keep-awake toggle - and the same K2.6 weights are already runnable on-device through Unsloth's 2-bit dynamic quant, so the local-execution story is not aspirational. The shared move is that long-horizon autonomy is being re-architected around a durable execution substrate that survives the session, and the contest is consolidating around who owns that substrate rather than who has the better model. The forward thesis is that this durable agent-execution layer stops being two vendors' bespoke plumbing and hardens into a named, expected primitive that a buyer assumes any serious coding-agent product ships. The concrete, falsifiable landing: by H1 2027 at least one additional major lab or coding-agent harness (the strongest candidates being Anthropic, Google, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Cognition/Devin, or a frontier Chinese lab such as Alibaba/Qwen, DeepSeek, or Zhipu) ships - as a documented, generally available product feature, not a preview teaser or blog mention - EITHER a durable cloud-sandbox execution mode where an agent task continues running and is resumable after the user's client disconnects or the local machine is shut down, OR a packaged local persistent-agent runtime that runs a multi-agent swarm on the user's own machine with scheduled/overnight execution and resumable long-horizon runs. A pure model-capability release with no durable-execution surface, a chat product that merely lengthens a single in-session run without disconnect survival or resumability, or a closed private beta with no GA path does not count; the marker is a third independent shipped durable-execution substrate (cloud-sandbox or local-swarm) beyond OpenAI/Ona and Moonshot/Kimi Work. If by June 30, 2027 no additional major lab or harness has shipped such a generally available durable-execution mode and the pattern remains confined to these two vendors, the prediction fails.

reasoning.because: OpenAI bought Ona for persistent cloud sandboxes; Moonshot shipped local-swarm Kimi Work (Jun 11-12)
reasoning.given: the agent contest is shifting from model quality to who owns the restart-surviving execution layer
reasoning.so_that: a third major lab or harness ships a generally available durable-execution substrate - cloud-sandbox or local-swarm
reasoning.landing: by H1 2027: a 3rd lab/harness ships cloud-sandbox or local-swarm durable agents
reasoning.plain_language: Two AI makers just shipped robots that keep working after you close your laptop; soon a third copies the idea as a normal feature.

summary: OpenAI's June 11 Ona buy (persistent cloud sandboxes) and Moonshot's June 12 Kimi Work (a 300-agent local swarm) split coding agents on where they run, moving the contest to who owns the restart-surviving execution layer. Expect a third major lab or harness to ship that durable substrate by H1 2027.
